title: Contract Status for Billing Rules
description: Workbench form for bulk-updating milestone and unit-of-delivery billing line statuses across multiple contracts in a single confirmed transaction.

objects.name: ProjParameters_AXM_APAVE_Extension

patterns.title: Pattern — Convenience helper on a table extension
patterns.body: When a feature is gated by a field on a parameters table, avoid repeating the field lookup across every call site. Add a named static method to the table extension so all callers go through one compile-checked point.

codeBlocks.label: X++ — Table extension static helper

callouts.title: What this achieves
callouts.body: A single named entry point for reading the flag. Any caller writes ProjParameters::isAutomatizeContractStatusEnabled() — readable, refactor-safe, and easy to find with cross-reference. If the field name ever changes, only this method needs updating.

callouts.title: Reuse this pattern whenever
callouts.body: Any feature flag, parameter field, or configuration value that is checked in more than one place. One method, one field reference, one place to change.

patterns.title: Pattern — Security-driven visibility on a form control
patterns.body: When a control exists on a form the user already has access to, but the control itself should only be visible or editable based on a specific security privilege, use a PostHandlerFor on the form init combined with SecurityRights to drive the control's visible() and allowEdit() properties at runtime.

codeBlocks.label: X++ — PostHandlerFor driving control visibility

callouts.title: What this achieves
callouts.body: The control is invisible to users without View access — they cannot see it exists. Users with View but not Edit see it but cannot change it. Only users with Edit access can toggle it. All of this without touching the standard form's AOT design.

callouts.title: How PostHandlerFor works
callouts.body: PostHandlerFor runs your static method automatically after the target form method completes. args.getThis() returns the live FormRun instance — so you get a reference to the actual open form, its controls, and its current state. No override, no CoC chain needed.

callouts.title: How SecurityRights works
callouts.body: SecurityRights::construct() gives a snapshot of the current user's effective permissions. formControlAccessRight(formStr, identifierStr) returns an AccessRight enum value for that specific control. Compare with >= — so >= AccessRight::Edit also covers FullControl.

callouts.title: ⚠️ Always null-check the control
callouts.body: If a future update renames or removes the control, formRun.control() returns null rather than throwing. Without the null guard, the form fails to open entirely. Always guard control lookups by name.

patterns.title: Pattern — Menu item gated by a database parameter
patterns.body: D365 security handles privilege-based visibility automatically. It cannot conditionally hide a menu item based on a database flag. To add a second condition — such as a parameters table toggle — subscribe to the SysMenuNavigationObjectFactory delegate.

codeBlocks.label: X++ — Delegate subscription for menu item visibility
codeBlocks.code: final class UpdateContractStatusBRVisibilityManager { [SubscribesTo( classstr(SysMenuNavigationObjectFactory), staticdelegatestr(SysMenuNavigationObjectFactory, checkAddSubMenuDelegate)), Hookable(false)] internal static void menuItemVisibilityHandler( SysDictMenu _rootMenu, SysDictMenu _subMenu, SysBoxedBoolean _subMenuVisibility) { if (_subMenu.isMenuItem()) { var meta = _subMenu.GetMenuItemMetaElement(); if (meta != null) { switch (meta.Name) { case menuItemDisplayStr(APV_UpdateContractStatus): _subMenuVisibility.value = ProjParameters::find().APV_AutomatizeContractStatus == NoYes::Yes; break; } } } } }

callouts.title: What this achieves
callouts.body: The menu item disappears from navigation entirely when the parameter is OFF — not greyed out, fully hidden. Both conditions must be true for it to appear: parameter ON and privilege assigned. The delegate handles the parameter side; D365 handles the privilege side automatically.

callouts.title: How the delegate works
callouts.body: checkAddSubMenuDelegate fires for every menu item the framework renders during navigation build. _subMenuVisibility is a boxed boolean passed by reference — setting .value = false removes the item. The switch on meta.Name lets one class cover multiple menu items cheaply. Hookable(false) prevents CoC wrapping.

callouts.title: 🚨 This is not a security control
callouts.body: This delegate only hides the item from the UI. A user who constructs the direct URL can still navigate to the form. Real access control comes from the security privilege on the menu item in AOT. Never use this pattern as a substitute for a privilege.

patterns.title: Pattern — Multi-select lookup on a string control
patterns.body: SysLookupMultiSelectCtrl wraps an existing FormStringControl and gives it multi-selection behaviour at runtime. No new AOT control type is needed. The controller stores the selection internally and returns a container of RecIds via get().

subSections.title: Lazy initialization
subSections.body: The controller is built on first need, not in init(). This avoids the control not yet being available during early form lifecycle methods.

codeBlocks.label: X++ — Lazy init with double null guard
codeBlocks.code: private void apv_ensureMultiSelect() { if (multiSelectCtrl != null) return; // already built — free exit FormStringControl contractIdCtrl = this.control(this.controlId('APV_ContractId')) as FormStringControl; if (contractIdCtrl == null) return; // control not ready yet — caller will retry Query q = new Query(); QueryBuildDataSource qbds = q.addDataSource(tableNum(ProjInvoiceTable)); qbds.addSelectionField(fieldNum(ProjInvoiceTable, ProjInvoiceProjId)); qbds.addSortField(fieldNum(ProjInvoiceTable, ProjInvoiceProjId)); multiSelectCtrl = SysLookupMultiSelectCtrl::constructWithQuery( element, contractIdCtrl, q); }

callouts.title: Why lazy and not in init()
callouts.body: During init() the form controls may not yet be fully rendered — calling controlId() too early returns 0 and the cast to FormStringControl returns null silently. Deferring to first use guarantees the form is ready. The first null guard makes every subsequent call free — no rebuild, no second query.

callouts.title: How constructWithQuery works
callouts.body: The query defines what appears in the multi-select dropdown. The controller binds to the string control and takes ownership of its lookup event. When the user opens it, the controller runs the query and renders a checkbox list. Selected RecIds are held internally — the string control only shows the display labels.

subSections.title: Resolving RecIds to business key strings
subSections.body: After the user confirms a selection, multiSelectCtrl.get() returns a container of RecIds. These are resolved back to ProjInvoiceProjId strings and stored for use in the data source query range.

codeBlocks.label: X++ — apv_resolveSelectedContractIds()
codeBlocks.code: public void apv_resolveSelectedContractIds() { container result; container selectedRecIds; ProjInvoiceTable projInvoiceTable; m_selectedContractIds = conNull(); this.apv_ensureMultiSelect(); if (multiSelectCtrl == null) return; selectedRecIds = multiSelectCtrl.get(); // container of RecIds for (int i = 1; i <= conLen(selectedRecIds); i++) { select firstonly ProjInvoiceProjId from projInvoiceTable where projInvoiceTable.RecId == conPeek(selectedRecIds, i); if (projInvoiceTable.ProjInvoiceProjId) result += [projInvoiceTable.ProjInvoiceProjId]; } m_selectedContractIds = result; }

callouts.title: Why resolve to strings and not keep RecIds
callouts.body: The data source query range filters on ProjInvoiceProjId — the natural business key — not on ProjInvoiceTable.RecId. Storing strings means the range-building logic is clean and each value is directly usable in SysQuery::value() calls without a join.

subSections.title: Applying the selection as a query range
subSections.body: The data source executeQuery() applies a different range strategy depending on how many contracts are selected.

codeBlocks.label: X++ — Three-strategy range in executeQuery()
codeBlocks.code: if (conLen(m_selectedContractIds) == 0) m_oRangeContract.value(SysQuery::valueEmptyString()); // show nothing else if (conLen(m_selectedContractIds) == 1) m_oRangeContract.value(conPeek(m_selectedContractIds, 1)); else m_oRangeContract.value( element.apv_buildMultiValueRange(m_selectedContractIds)); super(); element.clearCache(); element.refreshTotals();

callouts.title: Why three cases
callouts.body: The zero case is critical — an empty range string would show all records, not nothing. SysQuery::valueEmptyString() produces a special value the engine interprets as match-nothing, resulting in an empty grid. This prevents accidental mass operations on unfiltered data.

callouts.title: How comma-separated ranges work
callouts.body: Setting a QueryBuildRange value to a comma-separated string like "C-001,C-002" translates to SQL IN ('C-001','C-002'). SysQuery::value(str) wraps each value in the correct quote format for the engine.

patterns.title: Pattern — Edit method as a two-way grid binding with staged writes
patterns.body: An X++ edit method is a computed column on a form grid that supports both reading and writing. The framework calls it with _set = false to get the display value and _set = true when the user edits the cell. All writes must go to an in-memory buffer — never to the database directly.

subSections.title: Write branch — validation and buffer staging

codeBlocks.label: X++ — edit method write branch
codeBlocks.code: if (_set) { if (_contractLine.LineType != PSAContractLineType::UOD) return 0; // column does not apply to this line type Qty invoiced = PSAContractLineItemsServer::getContractLineInvoicedUnitsForUOD(_contractLine.ContractLineNum); Qty remaining = _contractLine.Units - invoiced; if (remaining < 0) remaining = 0; if (_value > remaining) { warning(strFmt("@apv_:ExceedsMaxAllowedMsg", _value, remaining)); return remaining; // clamp — don't reject } if (_value < 0) { warning("@apv_:NegativeValueMsg"); return 0; } // Stage in buffer — not written to DB APV_PSAContractStatusFormState state = APV_PSAContractStatusFormState::getOrCreate(element); state.apv_unitsReadyBuffer.insert(_contractLine.RecId, _value); return _value; }

callouts.title: 🚨 Never write to the database inside an edit method
callouts.body: Edit methods are called on every grid refresh — sometimes multiple times per repaint. Writing to the DB here causes unintended commits on every scroll or selection change. All changes must be staged in an in-memory buffer and committed only after explicit user confirmation.

callouts.title: Why clamp instead of reject on overrun
callouts.body: Returning the clamped value snaps the cell to the maximum rather than showing stale data. The user sees the corrected value immediately and the warning explains why. Rejection would require the user to clear and retype, which is worse UX for a validation that has an obvious correct answer.

subSections.title: Read branch — three-level priority
subSections.body: When the framework requests a display value, the method checks three sources in priority order before computing a default.

codeBlocks.label: X++ — edit method read branch
codeBlocks.code: else { if (_contractLine.LineType != PSAContractLineType::UOD) return 0; APV_PSAContractStatusFormState state = APV_PSAContractStatusFormState::getOrCreate(element); // Priority 1: pending edit from this session if (state.apv_unitsReadyBuffer.exists(_contractLine.RecId)) return any2Real(state.apv_unitsReadyBuffer.lookup(_contractLine.RecId)); // Priority 2: saved but not yet invoiced log entry PSAUnitsUpdateLog unitsUpdateLog; select firstonly AdditionalUnits from unitsUpdateLog where unitsUpdateLog.ContractLineNum == _contractLine.ContractLineNum && unitsUpdateLog.IsProposal == NoYes::No && unitsUpdateLog.IsInvoiced == NoYes::No; if (unitsUpdateLog.AdditionalUnits) return unitsUpdateLog.AdditionalUnits; // Priority 3: computed default — remaining = contracted - invoiced Qty invoiced = PSAContractLineItemsServer::getContractLineInvoicedUnitsForUOD(_contractLine.ContractLineNum); Qty remaining = _contractLine.Units - invoiced; return remaining < 0 ? 0 : remaining; }

callouts.title: Why three priorities
callouts.body: Without priority 1, pending edits vanish on every grid refresh because the buffer is not checked. Without priority 2, a value saved in a previous session disappears when the form is reopened. Priority 3 is the safe default for a line never touched — show what is left to invoice rather than zero.

patterns.title: Pattern — Singleton form state for pending edits
patterns.body: When multiple components of a form — edit methods, button handlers, data source methods — all need to share the same unsaved state, a singleton class acts as the single source of truth for that session.

codeBlocks.label: X++ — Session singleton with getOrCreate
codeBlocks.code: class APV_PSAContractStatusFormState { public Map apv_markAsCompletedBuffer; // RecId → 1/0 public Map apv_unitsReadyBuffer; // RecId → real public Set apv_lockedRecIds; // pre-fetched locked lines private static APV_PSAContractStatusFormState instance; public void new() { apv_markAsCompletedBuffer = new Map(Types::Int64, Types::Enum); apv_unitsReadyBuffer = new Map(Types::Int64, Types::Real); apv_lockedRecIds = new Set(Types::Int64); } public static APV_PSAContractStatusFormState getOrCreate(FormRun _formRun) { if (instance == null) instance = new APV_PSAContractStatusFormState(); return instance; } }

callouts.title: What this achieves
callouts.body: Any method anywhere in the form reads and writes the same buffers via getOrCreate(element). Pending edits survive grid refreshes, data source re-queries, and selection changes because they live entirely outside the grid. There is no risk of two separate copies of state diverging.

callouts.title: Why static is safe here
callouts.body: The static instance lives for the lifetime of the AOS session thread that opened the form. Each user opening the form gets their own thread — no cross-user contamination. When the form closes, the thread is released and the static variable goes with it. This would not be safe in a batch class or a shared service.

callouts.title: ⚠️ Clear buffers after every commit
callouts.body: After a successful commit, remove the submitted RecIds from both buffers. If you skip this, the edit method read branch returns the old staged value on the next refresh instead of reading the freshly committed database value — the grid appears not to have updated.

patterns.title: Pattern — Batch pre-fetch for lock detection
patterns.body: When rows in a grid need to be checked for a condition that requires a database query, never query per row. Pre-fetch all results in one set-based query before the loop and use an in-memory Set for O(1) lookup inside the loop.

subSections.title: Single-row variant
subSections.body: Use only when checking one isolated row — for example inside an edit method guard. Never inside a loop.

codeBlocks.label: X++ — Single-row lock check
codeBlocks.code: public static boolean isLineLocked(PSAContractLineItems _line) { ProjProposalOnAcc proposalLine; ProjProposalJour proposalJour; select firstonly RecId from proposalLine where proposalLine.PSAContractLineNum == _line.ContractLineNum join proposalJour where proposalJour.ProposalId == proposalLine.ProposalId && proposalJour.ProjInvoiceId == ''; // empty = unposted return proposalLine.RecId != 0; }

callouts.title: What makes a line locked
callouts.body: A line is locked when it is referenced by a ProjProposalOnAcc record whose parent ProjProposalJour has an empty ProjInvoiceId. Empty means the proposal exists but has not been posted to a real invoice yet. Once posted, ProjInvoiceId is populated and the line is no longer locked.

subSections.title: Batch variant — always use this in loops

codeBlocks.label: X++ — Pre-fetch then Set.in() inside loop
codeBlocks.code: // Called ONCE before the loop Set lockedRecIds = APV_PSAContractStatusHelper::preFetchLockedRecIds(contractIds); while (listEnum.moveNext()) { RecId recId = listEnum.current(); if (lockedRecIds.in(recId)) // O(1) hash lookup — no DB call { warning(strFmt("@apv_:UnpostedInvoiceProposalMsg", line.ContractLineNum)); continue; } // process the line... }

callouts.title: 🚨 Never call isLineLocked() inside a loop
callouts.body: With 1,000+ billing lines, calling isLineLocked() per row generates 1,000+ database round trips. The form becomes unusably slow and can timeout. Always call preFetchLockedRecIds() once before the loop, then use Set.in() inside it.

patterns.title: Pattern — Staged commit with confirmation dialog
patterns.body: No data is written until the user explicitly confirms. The button handler stages and validates, shows a summary dialog, then hands a fully-assembled commit buffer to the service layer. The service owns the transaction. This keeps ttsbegin/ttscommit out of UI code entirely.

flowSteps.title: MultiSelectionHelper iterates the grid selection
flowSteps.body: Counts milestone and UOD lines. Populates state buffers with defaults for any line not yet manually edited in the session.

flowSteps.title: Box::yesNo() — confirmation with counts
flowSteps.body: Shows a summary of what will change before anything is written. If the user clicks No, the method returns immediately with no side effects.

flowSteps.title: APV_PSAContractStatusBuilder::buildCommitBuffer()
flowSteps.body: Merges the two state buffers into a single typed Map<RecId, APV_PSAContractStatusCommit>. Only RecIds in the current grid selection are included — edits to unselected lines are ignored.

flowSteps.title: APV_PSAContractStatusService::validateAndUpdate()
flowSteps.body: Opens ttsbegin/ttscommit. Updates ProjOnAccTrans.IsMilestoneComplete for milestone lines. Calls PSAContractLineItemsServer::updateUODUnits() for UOD lines. Any unit overrun calls ttsabort — the entire batch rolls back.

flowSteps.title: Post-commit cleanup
flowSteps.body: Removes committed RecIds from both state buffers. Calls research(), clearCache(), and refreshTotals() to bring the grid and footer back in sync with the database.

callouts.title: Why the transaction lives only in the service
callouts.body: Button handler code deals with UI — dialog boxes, selection iteration, buffer population. Mixing ttsbegin into UI code risks holding a transaction open while waiting for user input, which locks records. The service receives a complete, UI-free commit buffer and opens and closes the transaction in the tightest possible scope.

callouts.title: ⚠️ ttsabort rolls back the entire batch
callouts.body: If any single UOD line fails the overrun check, the whole batch is aborted — not just that line. A partial commit would leave some lines updated and others not, with no indication of which. Fail all or commit all.

callouts.title: ✅ Neither privilege touches ProjTable
callouts.body: The customization is intentionally scoped to billing rule management only. Users cannot use these privileges to modify the project itself — the privileges have no relation to ProjTable.
